entry.title: A few assorted thoughts about LLMs in November 2026
entry.content:
• LLMs are useful tools. They're also the products of the greatest theft of intellectual labor in human history. Both of these things can be true at the same time.
  • In the right hands, LLMs can produce good, reliable software in shorter timeframes than ever before. Most hands are not the right hands. Most organizations using LLMs to write code are producing slop, no matter what they tell you in their press releases.
  • If you've never built serious software using an LLM, I urge you to make an honest attempt before you complain about them. You might be surprised.
  • If you're not using LLMs for code reviews—especially when it comes to security—you're not doing your job right.
  • LLMs over-engineer everything. Constantly pushing back against their eagerness to write code is exhausting and frustrating.
  • Software built entirely or partially using LLM assistance is fine, actually.
  • If an LLM-generated codebase has a security breach, the fault lies completely and fully with the human who generated and shipped that code. We must not allow AI to become yet another accountability sink.
  • If you use LLMs for writing—emails, text messages, blog posts, anything at all—please don't talk to me. Ideally, don't even sit next to me on the train. I don't want to associate with people who can't use their own words to communicate.
  • We ought to pass regulations that force the big AI labs to make all their training data public. This should include post-training data, too. Since most of the data used for training LLMs has been acquired unethically by ravaging our digital commons, it stands to reason that it should be released back into the commons.
  • The AI bubble does’t feel very bubbly to me. The big labs seem to be on the path to profitability. They might stop growing as fast as they're growing, but I don't expect a complete collapse. Source: vibes.
  • Models need to get faster. Like, 10-20x faster than they are currently. That's going to be the next inflection point for productivity. I don't want a bigger, smarter model. I want today's model to go brrrrr. Bonus points if it can be cheaper, too.
  • Has somebody figured out continuous learning yet? Is somebody working on it?
  • Open models will not eat Anthropic/OpenAI's lunch. The big labs will always have one thing your M9 MacBook Pro Max with 256GB RAM won't: infinite compute. That means they can always serve larger models than you can run at home. They can also serve small models at stupid fast speeds. There will always be workloads that require the largest models, and workloads that require smaller models burning more tokens faster. For example, certain long-horizon tasks like the Millennium Prize problems or finding holes in the Linux kernels both respond better to larger models and more token use.
  • The big labs are in the business of selling compute, not intelligence.
  • Dario and Sam do not have your best interests at heart. Be careful.
  • You should keep writing code by hand. You should keep learning computer science. You should have projects where you do not allow yourself to use any LLM assistance. Why? For the love of it, of course. But also to stay sharp, to understand how the sausage is made, to get close to the machine, and to make sure you're never fully dependent on silicon for your cognitive needs.

entry.title: How to categorise food in a way that is non toxic
entry.content:
I am happy that people are now more aware of what they are putting in their bodies. This has been a welcome change in India because we definitely have a nutrition problem.

Tracking calories and eating enough of every food group is a great way to stay healthy.

That being said IMO there is a way for this to get toxic. I have an opinion that most people are training like bodybuilders who are competing for the sport and that's not a great way to go about your fitness journey.

If you are someone who is training for the sport of bodybuilding, you will have to track every single kind of food which is going into your body down to the amount of salt in grams.

This is a simple way to get body dysmorphia. I feel like it is almond mom adjacent. Unfortunately I see this all the time in amateurs who are trying to lose weight as fast as possible before fight week. It's not healthy.

While I respect the sport of bodybuilding, I am very much sick of people who are doing it overwhelming my feed on algorithmic platforms. These people are well intentioned but are causing a damage which I consider to be invisible in most cases.

You don't need to eat like a bodybuilder to be healthy. More importantly you need to maintain a baseline amount of happiness while losing weight and gaining muscle. This doesn't need to be an excercise in misery, and believe me when I tell you this people in the sport of bodybuilding are miserable when they're actively training for competition.

The mindset shift which I have adopted is simple. I track my macros diligently and just eat enough.

I categorise food as:

  • necessary food

  • fun food

Necessary food is the type of food I need to stay healthy. Food like whole grains, tofu, animal protein. Anything which is not deep fried. Fresh salads come to mind. I am very flexible when it comes to this category, because I want to eat more of these necessary foods. Foods which are high in protein and fiber. Meals which are quick to make and easy to eat. Not overly high in calories and high in satiety.

Fun food is the food which I am eating when I am outside, anything fried, spicy or fizzy. It's stuff I eat when I am socializing or when I'm in the mood. You don't eat fun food all the time because then it's not fun it becomes mundane. These are calorie bombs which i need to earn on the weekends after a nice long run. Considering it to be a celebration of the week of exercise.

The reason why I am trying to have these categories is because I have seen over the years the conversation around health and fitness always tries to demonize certain food groups or foods. There is no such thing as good or bad food, there is just food. I think using moderation and good judgement is a great way to maintain a healthier diet.

By having these negative categories and demonizing eating, you are creating an atmosphere of toxicity and guilt. This is not really a great way to have a sustainable diet. I understand that everything needs to be done in moderation of course and the necessary and fun categories make it easier for me in my head to maintain my diet. Hopefully it makes sense to you the way it does for me.

Most of my meals are necessary, and on the weekends I can indulge a little and enjoy some fun food.

I don't want to get an eating disorder and by practicing what I preach hopefully I am able to make an impact on the people who I meet who might be struggling on their journey of health and fitness. Because I lost 20 kgs just following this simple protocol. I plan on losing 10 more.

This needs to be done in a manner where I can do this reliably over a long period of time.

You don't need to overcomplicate your diet at the end of the day it's calories in and calories out. Just maintain your macros and you are golden.

entry.title: Cars 2 Makes Sense.
entry.content:
Cars 2 has always been treated as the ugly duckling in the Cars franchise. I'm here to defend it. I think this film is the most logical next step you could have taken without playing it safe.

To write the first Cars film, the weird geniuses in Pixar went out to find all the different ways that cars affected our life.

The first film is feverishly devoted to vehicles, it's about (fictional) racing history rooted in real racing history. It's about settlements that get bulldozed over in the name of progress (quite literally by a bypass). Everything is derived from first principles about trying to do right by the concept of cars. The clouds are tire tracks. The bugs are cars. Everything is Cars. Even God.

Now, if we think about this, there are only three major ways that cars have manifested in media:

  1. The racing film (Your Days Of Thunder, Speed Racer, fast cars competing in high octane sports)
  2. The spy film (The Cool Car in every James Bond film, The getaway car, the car that saves the day, the Aston Martin DB5)
  3. The Fast And The Furious (I love whatever the hell they are)

If we take this premise and we have explored all that you can that sounds like a first-order effect of a world of Cars… how would you make a sequel?

A sequel needs to do two things for me to be a good sequel:

  1. It needs to be expand on the central theme of the franchise
  2. It needs to take the story forward in a new direction (no rehash, no Star Wars Episode VII)

Let's say you've made a beloved movie about anthropomorphized cars. Kids all around the world love them. What could you make that is a sequel that kids would still love while not betraying the root theme of your story?

Spies. Spies are so damn cool. The spy car is intrinsically awesome. There's so much novelty in a car chase with a car that's fitted out with all these cool contraptions to get away from people chasing them or something else. James Bond is of course the template, and they make it a point to bring out a new car with a new toy in almost every film. Even films that parody James Bond don't forget about the car. James Bond's car is as vital to James Bond as a shaken vodka martini.

If you're with me so far, If spies were to be the natural next step for your film about cars, then you'd need an evil moustache twirling villain with a political allegiance. Enter Professor Z, a vaguely Russian monocled Car that has been downtrodden all his life. This evil moustache twirling villain is an oil baron, making faulty alternative fuel to steer public outlook away from alternative fuel to line up his pockets and also he's trying to kill the Queen Of England.

What could be more James Bond than that?

Now how do we do this without betraying the core of the story? The story is still about McQueen and Mater's friendship. It's about McQueen underestimating Mater and not respecting his friendship. McQueen is still a racer, but the genius of the framing is that he's a celebrity target for the spy plot that this film is oriented around. It's about Mater's self-actualization beyond just McQueen's friend.

The best part of all this is that the folks at Pixar COMMIT to the decision.

Michael Giacchino's score for Finn McMissile is so effortlessly cool at emulating the vibes of a James Bond esque film. The plot beats match so perfectly with a traditional spy film. This film is such a loveletter to the genre.

Given all this context, let's examine Cars 2 as a sequel:

  1. Completely new direction? YES
  2. True to the core theme of friendship? YES

This film rocks.

Cars 3 on the other hand is cowardice while still being a pretty good film.

P.S. - I am also grateful for Cars 2 introducing weaponry into the Cars franchise because the movie tie-in game is so much fun. I love shooting up my friends and racing around. It's a delightful time all around.

Thanks to Nikhil for the lively discussion that inspired this blog post.

entry.title: License Cannot Beat Politics
entry.content:
Are there limits to the free software movement/ideology? It appears like there are

There’s a point that Pirate Praveen keeps repeating in FSCI chat group. It took me some years to understand. And there are several others who have not understood it yet. I quote:

my point is, trying to project ethics beyond copyright law into software only confuses people. Ethical movements should not be centered around software, trying to change the world through software licenses is a futile excercise, it only alienates potential allies but don’t actually achieves goals beyond what copyright law provides. Free Software works because it is within copyright laws limits. Community CoC works because communities can enforce its rules within their communities. The moment you want to enforce something beyond your community, you need political power and no software, however named or defined can povide you that. It is a naive/wishful thinking/illusion.

~ Pirate Praveen

If you need some explanation, you can read my post titled Give up the Free Software vs Open Source Debate where I try to explain the reality that free software and open source are functionally equivalent in politics (although in rhetoric free software movement sounds like it is much more political).

The free software movement (or the open source movement) does not operate as a political movement. It doesn’t participate in elections or try to influence political processes. It doesn’t have that many political goals. It doesn’t have cadre. It doesn’t have much literature around it (apart from the early GNU essays). It doesn’t have university professors teaching it as a political philosophy. It is nothing compared to political movements like Marxism, anti-caste movement, feminism, etc.

Yet free software movement (or open source movement) perpetuates itself. How?

The answer is that the free software movement (or the open source movement) is built on a hack. It is built by hacking into copyright. Copyright is a legal mechanism that’s enforced by the might of nation states. And by the clever loophole of using copyright itself to ensure free sharing, it was possible to unlock a peculiar game (like game of life). In this game, production of free software leads to production of more free software. And thus it creates value for everyone. And that’s how the free software movement (or the open source movement) survives/thrives.

PP says, therefore, that adding any political goal on top of the free software movement is unsustainable. Because there’s no mechanism through which such a goal can be achieved.

For comparison, take a movement like the feminist movement. You could add a political goal like “harassment free workspaces” to it. Feminists will then talk among each other and start mobilizing resources and attention towards campaigns like #MeToo. There’ll be widespread awareness about the issue and soon the goal will be achieved. This is what political movements are capable of achieving.

But for free software movement (or open source movement), there’s no such possibility of mass mobilization towards a political goal — because it has never built itself as a political movement.

You might think that the widespread adoption of code of conduct in free software communities is an example of such mass mobilization. It is, indeed. But it was the result of a mass mobilization by the feminist/LGBTQ+ political movements, not by a mobilization of the free software movement.

Even if we assume that there is a group of free software queer feminists who are political in both ways (free software and otherwise), their influence cannot be on the wider free software movement. They are limited by the subset of free software movement which is populated by such similar free software queer feminists. And one could even argue that their solidarity is not even mediated by free software, rather it is feminism/queer politics that brings them together.

There’s one more damning criticism that can be made on the “political” vision of free software. In the above explanation, I agreed with Praveen and said that the copyright hack is what lets free software work.

But one can say that the copyright hack isn’t even necessary (at least now).

When capitalism understood the true business value of sharing code, they discovered the economic incentives to keep this movement going. That they created the “open source movement” may have served some strategic function in the past. But regardless of what name they used, they unlocked a whole new upgraded-3D-splashy level of the game. They figured out we can save/make money with open source.

If one is skeptical of free software movement, one could even say that it is the economic model unlocked by the open source movement that sustains the free software movement. Copyleft licenses are not even necessary now to keep this going. Or in other words, even the copyright hack no longer applies.

And that’s an even bigger reason why politics doesn’t survive in free software movement. There’s no space for political goals in business.

If one really cares about politics, they would have to build a political movement (more practically, they would have to join existing political movements).

If they somehow hang around in free software movement hoping for a political change, they’re on the wrong bus.

Post-script: It is this realization that made me stop spending energy in free software circles and start spending it elsewhere.

entry.title: What the Pho, Rosh? #3
entry.content:
My Vietnam travelogue series is fondly named WTP, Rosh. You can read the first part here, the second part here.

I got a call from my mum the night I landed that she did not find the wallet in my house despite searching in all the places I had mentioned it would be in. To my family of friends and M, this would be a surprise - Rosh misplacing her WALLET of all things? Nah! Too Type-A to do that. But to my mum? - this was not a surprise because she’s seen how aloof I was as a kid. And it has been hard to shake off that image no matter how hard I’ve tried. Maybe some parenting programming inside her automatically made a list of all skills her kid needs but did not exhibit growing up? 🤷🏻‍♀️

IDK - I just know that it either takes a very very long time or something dramatic (multiplied by 5) to change the skills on that list.

“Are you sure it’s not in your bags?” 

“You’re right, Ma! It’s actually in my bag - I wanted to try a social experiment to see if a stranger would pay for my ticket if I pretended to lose my wallet.” is what I wanted to say…

“Yes, Ma, I have checked it 5 times now.” is what I ended up telling the poor soul who actually would have liked a retirement from the “Finder-Of-Things” title.

“Seriya yosichu paaru, yenga vechcha?” (Think hard and tell me where you actually kept it).

Well, this was not rhetorical even though I have written it as such. She really was inviting me to think out loud. So I put on my detective hat and mapped out all the touch points:

  • Home

  • Taxi to airport

  • Airport trolley

  • Airport security

  • Flight to vietnam

  • Noi Bai Airport to Bus

“Hmm. The only other place it could possibly be in is the Bangalore airport” I said “because I checked the taxi thoroughly before shutting the door. And I had my wallet in hand when I was showing my ticket at the baggage drop counter.”

And I did not realise I activated the end of the think-out-loud invitation with those lines because I heard a disappointed, anxious, and a fairly high-pitched “Airport la ya vittae???” (YOU LEFT IT IN THE AIRPORT???)

After that, the defense-lawyer in me responded on my behalf “I said it is a possibility. Why would I deliberately leave it in the airport?” followed by a quick “Okay, leave it - I will ask M to check at home. Now, you tell me - how are you?”

Fun Facts about Kempegowda International Airport I did not know earlier:

  • They have a functioning Lost and Found department.

  • That department reads emails sent to the official ID.

  • They respond within a few hours of emailing, even if it is midnight Indian time.

  • They will ask for lots of evidence to verify if the item is truly yours, including pictures of your wallet which you scramble to get.
    Because who takes pictures of their wallet randomly?

  • Textual description of the contents inside your lost wallet are also accepted as evidence of ownership
    THANK YOU, Checklist!

  • Once they assign you as the owner of the item, you have 30 days to collect it from the airport.

  • They allow you to nominate someone to collect it on your behalf provided they show proof of being authorized by you.

Now, ask me how I learnt the said fun facts. 🤡

entry.title: Long time, no post!
entry.content:
It's been a while since I wrote here.

I've been busy.

I think I did nothing except work for a year. I definitely did not have any mental space to read, write or do anything else for myself.

On the bright side, I wrapped up work in July. I've been on a break since then. It was a conscious decision as I could see my mental health deteriorating. It has taken me time to recover and feel like myself. Apart from occasional identity crisis and panic, I am mostly good.

The first month was hard. I remember my body feeling panic on Saturday evenings and planning next week. On weekdays, I would not be calm in the evenings because I would be thinking about what meetings the next day is starting with. I had to actively pull myself out of this loop. Few weeks in, sadness crept in. I was technically free and despite having plenty of half-read books and drafts to finish, I could not focus. I had imagined that I'd use this break to create but I was not able to.

Those who know me would know that I have largely worked as a consultant in my career. I am no stranger to the lull in between projects. It used to cause me discomfort when I was in between work but a younger version of me did not understand the reason. The usual suspects would be not having work or a job, people around or even having money credited to your account on a regular basis(although this hurts differently 🥲). But more than anything, I liked being useful and needed.

So here is a bit about what I did manage to do:

  • I used this IKEA pouch to make a Sashiko embroidery pattern

  • Old Rubberband GRID notebook with a Cross Stitch Rose

  • Cyanotype experiments

  • Type workshop with Cyrus Highsmith

  • Zine about trees

  • Inktober

entry.title: What the Pho, Rosh? #2
entry.content:
My Vietnam travelogue series is fondly named WTP, Rosh. You can read the first part here.

Once I got off at the bus station, I did the most obvious thing I could think of - look for ATMs near me on the map. But once I started lugging my luggage a few steps, I realised the most obvious step would actually be to book a Grab to the Airbnb (as my Grab was paid for by card). For some reason, I didn’t have any luck with the taxis, so when a kind Grab scooter driver at the bus station asked if I wanted a ride, I negotiated and agreed.

If someone had taken a picture of us, this was how it would have looked.

Was taking a Grab scooter with 32KGs of luggage on my bingo card for Vietnam vacation? Definitely not. But technically I have dropped M off at the railway station pulling such stunts on a two wheeler during peak Bangalore traffic, so I knew this wasn’t too dangerous. As a result, when the Grab scooter driver suggested that I do this, he did not have to say too much to convince me. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

(There’s a reason I chose this title for this series, y’all.)

The driver dropped me off at the Airbnb, but I still don’t have any cash, remember? So I told him to take me to the nearest ATM, withdrew the cash from there and paid him. Maybe we can skip the part where he waited ten minutes to be paid for the five minute ride because I forgot my ATM pin and almost lost access to my Forex card? 𓁹‿𓁹

It was now 8AM Vietnam time.

Yes, all this had happened within 8AM on the day I landed.

I had arrived at the Airbnb tired and hungry and the host greeted me with hot water and a coffee pre-mix. This was the warmest welcome I had had since I landed. Not only did it stave off my hunger till I freshened up, but I finally felt like I was in the Coffee land.

And while I sat there sipping that coffee, the case of the missing wallet continued in my ever-anxious mind of mine.

entry.title: Weeknote 44 2026
entry.content:
Super duper late weeknote. Sorry for the delay, I was travelling back home and had underestimated how much time it takes to complete one weeknote entry!

Life

Back to hanging out with Kunwar

Ever since Gunwant has left, I wasn't able to hangout with Kunwar as much. After the Wayanad trip, I left for my hometown and upon return I kept getting pulled into random plans every Sunday. And hence, I feel very happy that I could watch Resident Evil with him last week and then we could go to Manjeet da Dhaba this Sunday. This restaurent was recommended to us by Tanvi and Ankur. Thanks a lot peeps for the banger recommendation!

While we were discussing about the place initially during the co-working session, it was brought up that this Dhaba is located in a super shady place. I mean yeah, it is under a bridge, which is a dead end and bridge is a foot bridge carrying passengers away from a railway station. Sounds like perfect recipe for disaster, but it felt chill mostly. I could see a bunch of young women using the bridge late in the night and surrounding seemed bustling too. It might have been shady before, but it definitely felt a lot safer now. Though as always, better safe than sorry.

Next up, I would like to try Kenneth's recommendation of another Punjabi restaurent he had sent over the DM :).

Movie night

Immediately after the dinner I cycled to Ayush's place for a movie night with climbing friends. This was a very last minute plan and hence, at a point, both me and Ayush were convinced it's just gonna be the two of us. Thankfully, everyone showed up slowly but surely. We watched Airplane. Mann, what a masterpiece, more about it in the movies section below!

Restaurent week

This Tuesday, in celebration of the Restaurent week, I went out with Aeish, Atharva, Kiran, Tanvi, Ankur for a lunch at Baan Pad Thai. This restaurent is on the path from metro station and climbing gym to my house, and hence I see it every single day. I have been meaning to go to this place for a while and hence when Tanvi asked about it on the co-working signal group, it was an instant yes from me!

Well, not thinking and answering yes instantly did cost me a bit, I only later realized that each seat for this set menu cost 2k rupees!! Zomato sneaked in a 600 rupees "convenience" fee too, what a rip off! We had one starter, one main course and one dessert. I think it would have been much cheaper to go individually, but I don't regret it. Though, there's a good chance I am not participating in restaurent week again for trying out a new place 🙈.

Food is reviewed in the section below.

After the nice lunch, we headed to Ondu for a freshening filter coffee. We had some really interesting talks here, I think what peaked my interest most was Tanvi talking about post-partition struggles to unite India as it is today. A lot of freedom fighters did in fact go villain mode to the opposing regions, and made them unite with the India!

Somehow, we got super lucky and had visited Ondu on their birthday, happy birthday! 🥳 They treated us with a 1 + 1 offer on coffee and then also gave us an on-the-house chocolate cake! So much sugar rush 😭.

Swimming and cycle

On Thursday morning, me and two other climbing friends decided to go swimming 🏊. I haven't swam in a while and that's why I was really looking forward to it.

I woke up early, cycled to the place and started calling them. Guess what, none of them picked up 😡. So here I was standing outside the swimming pool feeling betrayed and dejected. But then I realized I didn't care as such cause swimming itself is the mood uplifter for me! So that's what I did and honestly, I just felt at ease in the water. Only thing I like about the Halasuru swimming pool is they allow one to swim for the full hour, no whistles ringing at 40 minutes mark to come out and take shower.

Everything was amazing, and...another bad luck struck. When cycling back, my fender and brake support broke off the core cycle frame and flew off in the middle of the road 🙃. If it wasn't for my reflexes I would have done a full 180 with the cycle 😂. I somehow untangled the brake system and drove to the nearest cycle repair shop for a quick repair. I lost my fender to heavy cars, and I currently don't have any plans of re-installing one. Let's see if I do end up needing one in the future. Due to all this fiasco, I started my day at 12! Absolute disaster of a day.

Happy birthday Harsh

On Thursday evening, after climbing and scolding session, all of us celebrated Harsh's birthday in Si Nonna's. Happy birthday again Harsh 🥳!

Following the SUPER awesome dinner, we found ourselves at Rohan's house yapping about the most random topics, ranging from story behind Tulsi being a plant to japanese tentancle hentai 😭. We also ripped off a number plate from an abandoned Mercedes in Rohan's apartment. I wish I had similar level of presence of mind cause I would have loved to get one for decoration in my room.

Most of the people left, but four of us found ourselves having late night chai and shouting Contact at each other 😂. After almost getting chased out by the shopkeeper for shouting too loud, we decided to head home at 3 in the night.

Drink till death

On Friday evening, I agreed to a plan of drinking party at Chin Lung's with an ex-colleague of mine. I hadn't seen him in a while, and a bunch of current colleagues were going to drink with him, so I just decided to tag along. Most of the times I do not participate in these parties cause I don't like people who over drink and cause trouble. I hate having to clean up their mess!

Although everyone had agreed to only drink 2 shots, all of them ended at 10 shots each!! I have never seen 13k spent just on shots in Chin Lungs 😭. All of them were scolded by me into having warm water and salt + lemon at regular intervals. This prevented anyone from going mad and causing a ruckus and allowed us to have a pretty good time. At one point, we were dancing with all the people around our table, it was super fun!

I also learned about a secret to check salaries of newly joined people in our company. Overall, it was 👍 Great Success 👍.

Sleep cycle is MESSED UP

My messed sleep cycle has not recovered yet. Initially, it was Navratri keeping me up, but now it's hanging out with friends. Ever since shifting to Indiranagar, I am hanging out with all the different groups a lot more. But this week was top of the charts!

Hangouts plus an extremely bad habit I have developed of reading manga before bed. Contrary to what I am writing, most of the times this helps me go to sleep, but that also is dependent on the part of manga story I am currently reading. If it's the usual, then yeah definitely helpful! But there are sections in the story which get you riled up so hard! I am currently reading through one right now and it is a nightmare to sleep with SO MUCH ENERGY 😭.

Bengaluru Systems Meetup

On Saturday, I attended November edition of Bengaluru Systems Meetup. Theme this time was Inference. We had four interesting talks and I was accompanied by Samyak and Ayush for some interesting live discussion on the same xD.

First talk was around: How does inference actually work?. This could have been a banger talk. Sadly, presenter just rushed through it. Some topics in there easily deserved an individual talk of their own. It would be interesting to see a continually running deep dive into various parts of inference over few months.

Second talk was titled: One process, a hundred agents, or a harness written in Zig. This was given by a guy who doesn't work in tech, he's a finance bro! He got tired of how heavy the harnesses are in practice. All they need to do is loop over popen + curl.

Are there gaps in his harness? FOR SURE. Does it matter? Nope. My buddy is out here FAFO-ing, how can I not be impressed?

To be honest, I did shit about it with a mutual. And then the mutual asked me what was I expecting? Some peak perf ILP/MLP, no-cache-thwarting software?? I am the person who usually looks at things with optimism, I thank my mutual for reminding me that :).

Next up was The Interface Tax: How Much of Near-Memory Compute's Speedup Survives in LLM Decode?. Talk was around new architectures where memory and compute were right next to each other, and how layout-aware memory controllers could help mitigate a lot of issues we face today in CPU <> GPU world. One of the Q&A questions I liked a lot was: "How is this different than a GPU?". And honestly, at that moment I looked back at the whole talk and did not find a difference 🫠.

But I also walked away with validation of an idea I have brewing since a long time. Any HPA (high performance applications) needs:

  • Workload driven scheduling with full IO control
  • Workload driven hardware and memory control
    • Hard Disks
    • SSDs
    • Memory
    • S3, everything

Final talk was around One Kernel to Run Them All: Compiling LLMs into a Single Megakernel with Megabake. And honestly, I did not listen to this one, it was too dense for me 🙈.

Climbing

This was an awesome week in climbing! But sadly, I have no videos this time. Maybe it's a proof of how much I was engrossed in enjoying the climbs?

Sunday

I sent the level 6 green I was trying last week. As I had mentioned in the last weeknote, it was just me being exhausted. I should have tried that climb earlier in the session. This time, I tried it just after the warm up and it was my day's first attempt-first send!!

Next, we were trying out level 5 yellow on the slab wall. This was pain and tears. Whole route was so sketchy: standing on super small holds at weird angles, balancing yourself on a literal sloper hemisphere 😭. I finally gave up on the beta tall people had suggested me, and asked the comp kids about how they approach it. Btw, these are literal kids, some are not even 10 years old 😂. I am kinda proud of myself that I approach them with the curiosity to learn! Stay humble, keep learning. It also reminds me of this line from ascelpius's "Why I fight" blog: Leave your footwear and ego outside the door.

Tuesday

After loads and loads of sketchy falls, I finally sent the level 5 yellow!! I really wish I could have taken a video. But I also DO NOT want to repeat it. Every time I get on slab so sketchy, my heart rate shoots off the roof. Well, why do I still do it? I kinda like being scared and then overcoming that feeling by proving myself wrong :P.

Rest of the session was just time pass. Whatever I could do, I had done. In remaining climbs, I was aware of some fundamental work I had to do to unlock them. I was pretty sad near the end of the session. Not because I had finished only one climb, but because I wasn't tired 😮‍💨. I am so used to being dead by the end of the session that the day I am not, I feel super dissatisfied.

Thursday

This week, wall on the second floor got reset! There was also a competition called "Flash or Slash" happening. Basically flash routes in the order they have been marked, starting from level 1 till level 7.

I decided to not care about it cause I start climbing under pressure in competitions. I am happy enjoying climbing as it is. And this caused me to flash everything till level 5s, except this one level 3 slab style route which irritated me a bit too much. I was able to send it near the end of the session, but I absolutely hate routes like that.

As in for the level 5s, I was able to flash the red one with a lock off, heal hook beta. I also sent another purple slab in 2-3 attempts. Only one remaining was black lache jump which I was so close to sending and just slipped in the end move. Next time it is!

Surprisingly, I also almost got both level 6s too! With one move remaining in each one, I am hopeful about sending this set completely!

Food

Chinita

We had taken a small break between the climbing session on Sunday to grab some food. We headed to Chinita and ordered:

  • Tortillas
  • Nachos

Tortillas were straight up bad and Nachos were average-ish. I should stick to my default order here 😭.

Manjeet da daha

Thanks again to Tanvi and Ankur for suggesting this place! It was a banger recommendation.

We ordered:

  • Chana sabzi
  • Paneer and aloo parathe

I think all of us unanimously agreed Paneer sabzi was THE BEST! Not sure what was the preparation style, but it absolutely slapped. Chana sabzi was okay-ish, one of my Punjabi friends was talking about how it seemed to have the same preparation as all the Dhabas near his hometown. Parathe were easily much much better than Khao and Khaane do. Dal Makhni was okay-ish. And finally `kheer was average too.

So much average for a place I am calling banger. Well paneer, lassi and the price made up for everything. It was just 240 per person and we were brim full! Fully worth it.

Baan Pad thai

All of us ordered a bunch of stuff and I don't remember it all, so I am going to list out things I personally liked. Corn Fritters were absolute banger! Whatever sauce they had applied on it, elevated it to my top corn fritter place. Sadly a consistent theme you would find through all the dishes, quantity was pretty less :(.

I really liked Veg Pad thai noodles too! I wish I had ordered that instead of the Tom Yom rice in the photo above.

entry.title: three datemarts
entry.content:
[like other dmarticles, much of this is made up]

Three first dates.

First first date.

This was my first first date ever. K and I were going to the "rival" college for a fest. Notably, there was the The Local Train concert, her favourite band, scheduled for the evening.

The moment I stepped in the auto, it was clear I was the underdressed one. She was in goth black, and I was in hostel green. She laughed it off, having expected no better.

We knew we had to meet up with the rest of our college friends there, but we were in no hurry to do so. But we bumped into J, and she had only one thing on her mind. Chaat.

We walk to the chaat stall and have the dahi puris arranged. As J is yapping about some professor she's dealing with, K wraps her pinky fingers around mine under the table. And gives me a blank sideways glance. And then tugs.

J doesn't know that we are now dating. And that this is our first date. Neither do any of our other friends. They thought this matter was settled. K had already told them that she'd resolved to move on, after an year of realising that K-mart was not going to happen. Little did they know that I had asked her for this date, six long months after she had given up.

Second first date.

"Hey dmart, will you go to prom with me?" asked P, with a roguish flair. This wasn't real prom. This was her friends' dance and DJ party at a venue, where she helped connect and supply the talent. It had the theme of "prom."

I chuckle, acknowledging her bit.

"No really. You ruined my plan. I didn't know you were here. I left you a note in the kitchen, thinking you'd see it after I am gone. Go see it." I go to the kitchen, and there it was. The note intended for keeping track of our groceries now indeed had the scraggly letters: "HEY DMART. WILL YOU TAKE ME TO PROM. CALL ME [...] <3 P".

"So?"

Well... yeah. Of course.

My friend, N, who had witnessed this looked at me with a smugness, after P left the house.

"What?"

"I just... This is insane," she said as she grinned wider.

Okay, N, I am very rusty at this thing. I have only gone on a first date once, and that was like five years ago. Was I just asked out?

"You're a dumbass."

I still had the gall to text P, and ask her if she was flirting with me after that.

The moment I came back from work that Friday, I realised that I'm not really even the underdressed one—I'm not dressed at all for "prom." P was in a leopard-patterned shawl, that set off against her black tank top and leather skirt.

Well looks like I am a dumbass, I said. I thought prom was tomorrow. "What?!" she guffawed. Just come like this, it's fine. We have to get there in twenty minutes. I was already unpacking my stuff. That is enough time for me to change into prom, I said. Worry not.

Third first date.

R, the only person to have ever liked my Hinge profile, was a person who studied and enjoyed the arts. So, we went to the national gallery of modern art.

"Can we go to the mixed media wing? It's one of the few parts that I haven't yet seen thoroughly." It was my first time, so I was happy to go anywhichways. It was clear that I was the overdressed one. She was in flannel shirt and jeans, and I was in a short, bright blue kalamkari kurta and a tote bag slung around my shoulder to match the artsy pretension of the occasion.

We walk through the passage to the wing, which had an art piece of abstract-looking soldiers on horses, popping out of the canvas storming towards something. She stopped me, and walked up to it. Really close to it. Then bent with her hands on her knees to look at it from another angle. Then she walked slightly ahead, to look at it from the sides. A couple of quiet minutes had passed.

"Sorry, sorry," she said with a hint of trepidation, "I just like looking at art very closely. There is so much that you don't see when you just hurry past everything."

I was delighted at this. I can stand here all day, I told her. But tell me how you are looking at everything. I want to see as you do.

"Hey, your college has very tall buildings and shit. Ours is all flat, there's no nothing here that's over four floors. No one can really even kill themselves here."

I looked at this friend of friend, nodding. I glanced sideways at K and immediately realised that the both of us were looking for an open to get out of this conversation and plunge into the anonymity of crowds.

"Hey, what's down that slope?"
"No idea bro."
"Great, we'll go there and report back." I never saw that person ever again.

K was now feeling comfortable enough in this part of campus to wrap her arms around mine. She tugged me towards the large, flat shed, from where we heard a bit of laughter. There was a large crowd standing and facing the stage, completely obscured to us. Seems like we had snuck into an event without any tickets.

"Wait what? This is a comedy show?"
"Yeah, I can't see shit," said K.
"You're slightly taller. Maybe hop and you'll get a glance?"
"Oh wait," I realise, "It's that guy. He had that bit about Indian stray dogs. The one that I found kind of unfunny."

We walked out of that show, and sat on a bench not far outside it.

"Your phone is ringing," I said, "It's J. I think she's looking for us. She's probably at near the ground at the concert."
"No, you're sitting with me for a while." She proceeds to rest her head on my shoulder.
"Gosh, you really do look cute," she pauses and says, "in a bhayanak kind of way."

We enter the premises of the hotel where this prom event is happening. Before I even had the chance to glance at the tokens for redeeming the drinks, and people start flocking around P. She had an immensely strong gravitational field. Many hugs and greetings were exchanged with all these people I have never met before.

It was clear, that I was but a tiny satellite that newly entered her orbit. I was looked at as a curiosity, this total stranger who is now P's plus-one. P was doing fantastically well, introducing me as someone who was worthy of something more exciting than a P-plus-one, while also expertly diverting the flirtations of innumerous men who were unaware of this fact.

She picked up the menu when we got to the bar counter. I asked what caught her eye. She pointed to two of the drinks. Either this or that.

It has to be that. It has mezcal in it. I replied swiftly.

"Ooh, why do you like mezcal?"
"It tastes like smoke!" I place the order.
"Dmart. I'm not waiting for our drinks. Let's go dance."

"Wow, this detail is incredible." R was now dissecting this painting in a low tone, explaining to me how the artist might have made it. She tilted her head. I followed suit and tilted mine too. "You see it? Right there in the negative space."

"Woah, yeah. Wow. I totally missed that."
"Am I talking too much?"
"No. Please don't stop talking."

We go to the next one. I point to yet another horse in this painting.

"For some reason artists are fucking obsessed with horses."
"Maybe it will make for a good drinking game."

We go to the next one. Horse in the corner. Next one. Oh, this one has ten horses. Next one. That one is a ripped horse. Very good muscles. Oh another one there. Okay, this is actually getting ridiculous. We go to the next wing. We are giggling like idiots at every horse sighting in between the serious art dissection. Oh, the equestrian excesses.

I tap her shoulder when we get into the next gallery. Look behind you. She turns around, and folds into a suppressed fit of laughter. It's a massive, massive landscape by MF Husain, depicting five delirious, wide-eyed screaming horses.

We couldn't even get halfway through all the works on that floor before we were kicked out, because it was closing time for the gallery.

"Hey, before we part ways, I got you this. I think you'll like this?" I take out a couple of vintage Tamil records. "I don't know if you know these, it's carnatic s—"

"I love this. I know this." And then her eyebrows furrow, and she looks at me. "I don't think I can keep this, this is too good. No. And I didn't even get you anything."

"You helped me experience art galleries in a new way. That is priceless. These records are cheap. Please have them. I want you to have them."

"Wait, they are cheap?"

An hour later, we could be seen sitting on the floor of a local bookstore, with R, trawling through every single cheap, vintage record, giving each of them the same kind of attention as she was with the paintings. I was pleased hearing her describe the various classical works.

We were with our group of friends, enjoying The Local Train.

K looks at me. "I think we should go ahead," she said, wanting to get away from our dearest friends.

"Yeah, what if they play Choo Lo while we are all the way back here with these people?" I playfully tell her, having done my homework on the The Local Train discography, and her favourite songs from it.

I take her hand, and we slither all the way to the front of the stage. It is dark and moonlit, just enough to be able to see K's face.

The band plays the first few twangs of Choo Lo. K leaps in excitement, and holds me tight, while swaying and singing along.

[translated to english]

I am standing right here even today
Clinging to the hope of you
What is this helplessness?
What is this longing in my heart?

She looks straight into my eyes, when the chorus comes on. The whole ground is singing along.

You arе etched in my gaze
Just say it once
That you are mine—only mine
You are etched in my gaze

It settles into a bridge section.

I will remain like this. Just like this. Just like this.

I wake up next morning. P is in the living room. I see her looking a bit stressed out.

"I can't find my wicker basket. And I have to head back now."

It was a gift from her best friend, and it had immense sentimental value. I swing into action, already pocketing my keys. "It has to be at the venue. You go. I'll find it and keep it with me. You can get it from me when we meet again."

I went to the venue and I found it. I texted P the good news. When I got back, she had already left. There was another note on my table, in scraggly characters.

It said: "DMART, WE DRAW FISHES BECAUSE THEY EXIST. AND I'M LEAVING THIS NOTE BECAUSE YOU DO :D XOXO, P"

A couple of weeks, and a second date later. I call her.

As whimsically charming as P is, I tell her, a platonic friendship felt more right. She immediately agreed.

Outside the bookstore, I look at R, holding my tote bag which now has a few more records in it. She's wistfully looking down. "Hey, today was so much fun. Really."

"But, I don't know. I don't know if I'm ready for this. I have a lot going on in my life, and I may not have the capacity for this."

I ask her to take it as slow as she wants, and drop it any time.

"Today was fun, right?"
"Yeah."
"Then no matter what happens next, we have already won. No one can take away the fun we just had."

A couple of weeks, and two dates later. She calls me.

As nice as hanging out with me has been, she thinks she's just not ready for this emotionally. She takes up on my offer of dropping this any time. I oblige.

entry.title: The Geography of Shrinkage
entry.content:
You are whose homes you go to?

Someone recently called me local. The “placeness of you” they’d said. 

I guess when you live in a neighbourhood long enough, you are the tree you visit, the cats you scritch, the roads you know your phone gets snatched at, the dog poop you avoid, the plants you count on pavements, the smells of old buildings, and the people you walk to and away from.

Eight years in my Bangalore neighbourhood now, and I finally understand why my parents never left their Bombay home.

I moved to my little neighbourhood in Bangalore for a non-tech, life-changing job. Which, by Bangalore standards is crazy. My good ol’ neighbourhood is now full of tiny workplaces and too many people, but during my touchdown, we hardly had 1 chai shop, let alone a revenue stream. 

Rents were reasonable then, landlords surprisingly pre-psychotic. My first house was a dream. Me as a flatmate to my lovely two others, not so much. I had too much freedom, too much power, too much to process, and too little familiarity with personal space.

Bangalore can be a very isolating place without a clique. Miraculously, I started finding people who loved me within a few kilometres of my home, maybe, they found me, in a way that no neighbourhood in the vastness of Bombay ever offered.

Bids for connection turned into friendships, friendships into partnerships, partnerships into let’s-grow-old-togethers.

Being a moss on the wall of a neighbourhood you swore you'd be buried in often comes with a rare but also sweepingly common comfort you come to rely on.

Houses. Homes. So many homes and its incumbent couches to plonk yourself into.

How often I visited somebody's home in Bangalore often determined the depth of what I shared with them. In a city that's too expensive to stay outdoors and too infrastructurally disappointing to walk around in, you find yourself—if you're someone with the privilege to do this—spending a good amount of time inside people's homes.

This also comes with a flipside when you take up too much space in someone’s home.

I grew up in a joint family in a one-room kitchen in a Dadar B.D.D chawl. I never learnt personal space, but I thought I'd outgrown the need to learn it when I moved out of Bombay. But the way my body plonked itself into a kitchen that wasn’t mine as though it were—often indicated that I had many lessons in boundaries ahead of me.

One belongs in a space when they take their rightful place in it, with the people who inhabit it. If I try to be my friend's partner, I won't find belonging in that friendship. If I try to be my mum's friend, I won't find belonging as her child.

I will only belong when I take my rightful place with them.

I find the same is true of space-taking and home-hopping. I often wonder if I cloak myself in the shape of other people’s homes because I'm afraid of losing my internal one.

A friend’s most intense belonging formed within the four walls of his friend’s home. So visceral was the house's presence in his life-building, that he cried when they sold some of their furniture.

When his belonging moved out of the neighbourhood, he avoided entering their street for a whole year. The other day, I mentioned their apartment name to him and he said, "That's vaguely familiar," and gasped the second he realised what had happened.

Not remembering their home hit worse than not remembering they used to be together.

To be able to go over to someone’s home for tea instead of the neighbourhood café is not a mere convenience, it is how bids for deeper connection meet consent.

For a while, I had the time to build a friendship with someone whose home had made room for me. I felt like I had another physical space in which my body took up space.

Now, as the shape of how we arrange ourselves in each other's orbits changes, my access to their home is in flux. And my body physically shrinks a few blocks down their street. Like I'm physically realising that my hands are a little smaller than I thought they were.

When you have lesser and lesser homes, so achingly familiar, the places you've built yourself in, your body shrinks to reflect your smaller geography.

You contract more often, hunch over, curl up.

Is it a coincidence that I have developed posture-induced spinal issues now?

The topography of shrinkage is an emotional one.

There will no doubt be new walls to attach parts of me to, in the “localness”, “placeness” of me. New streets nobody who left you ever lived in. New diners to try in the multiplication of capitalistic cells in your charming village.

But even the river billowing to the sea, creating new silt along the way, doesn't lose memory of the dried-up, barren tributaries it left behind.

It trembles in the shrunken geography of its many graves.
